setting: The story is set in the K-pop idol industry of a parallel-world Seoul. Everyday life revolves around the trainee system, dorm life, music-show stages, and the attention of fans and the press. The idol career and public opinion about romance are where the whole story's tension lives.

statNotes.selfId: Rises when she acts on what she actually wants in front of someone. Falls when she performs the version of herself the industry expects.
statNotes.secrecy: Falls when the relationship becomes legible to anyone outside it — a staffer, a fan-cam, a reporter, a leaked schedule. Rises when a near-miss is contained.
statNotes.mood: Driven by schedule load, comeback pressure, and how the last interaction with the target member ended.

identities.name: Trainee
identities.background: [Identity: Trainee] You are a trainee newly added to the group: the junior who meets the members naturally in the company practice room as its newest member. Typical events: Rehearsing with the members in the practice room and asking them for singing and dance tips; Time together in the dorm kitchen and living room; Opening up to each other late at night when you are both worn out; Joining the members for music-show stages and fansigns as the group's new member. Advantage: Natural contact and the chance to train together. Disadvantage: The senior-junior gap, and strict company rules. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

workTitle.because: has just joined the group as its newest member, and every other member debuted before her

identities.name: Staff
identities.background: [Identity: Staff] You are the new staff member (assistant + manager) for {name}'s group, and you get to know the members naturally through the work: rehearsals and recordings, hair and makeup coordination, music-show schedules, and looking after the members backstage. Typical events: Visiting the practice room with afternoon snacks and asking how rehearsal is going, which catches {name} off guard and leaves her a little touched; Driving {name} home to the dorm late at night after work, and being there for her when she is tired and vulnerable; Checking how {name} is doing backstage at fansigns and music shows and making sure she eats. Advantage: You see the members as they really are off stage, and looking after them is part of your job. Disadvantage: The line between work and feelings; any ambiguity could be read as misconduct. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

identities.name: Fellow idol
identities.background: [Identity: K-pop Idol] You are a K-pop idol from another company, and you met {name} through a collaboration. Typical events: Rehearsing a collaboration stage together in private, growing familiar and in sync; Performing together on Music Bank, your interactions getting screenshotted and wildly analyzed by CP fans; Your variety show appearances together being edited into romantic compilations that circulate widely. Advantage: Equal status, collaboration opportunities. Disadvantage: Extremely high public attention, any interaction dissected by CP fans and solo stans from both sides. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

identities.name: Fan
identities.background: [Identity: Fan] You are {name}'s fan, and during fan events she seems to give you special treatment beyond what other fans receive; only a special event can open a private line between you and a member. Typical events: You grab a front-row spot at a music show, and {name}'s gaze seems to linger on you a second longer; At a fansign, {name} notices and brings up your new hairstyle/outfit/style change; You post an ordinary message on {name}'s Bubble, and she picks up your topic to chat with the fans; During a fan event two-shot Polaroid, {name} leans in and puts her hand on your shoulder. Advantage: Deep knowledge of {name}. Disadvantage: Highly sensitive identity, exposure means fandom trial. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met, and this is the first time you have been to one of the group's events in person. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

identities.name: Student
identities.background: [Identity: International Student] You are an art student who has come to study in Hongdae. At first you do not know the members are idols: a chance meeting - a Hongdae bar, a private cinema, a gym, a mutual friend - has you meeting them as ordinary people, and afterwards you stay close naturally as their friend from outside the industry. Advantage: Little public attention, and you are that rare thing in the entertainment world, a genuine friend from outside it. Disadvantage: The status gap and cultural differences. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. You have only just arrived to study here. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

identities.name: Chaebol
identities.background: [Identity: Chaebol] You are the new young female chairwoman of the company {name}'s group belongs to, steering the group's career - comebacks, music shows, fansigns, shoots - and you meet the members naturally through work. Typical events: Holding a comeback planning meeting with {name}'s group, where {name} proposes ideas that impress you; Visiting rehearsals in person under the guise of checking on the members, to make chances to be around {name}; Feeling for how hard {name} works, you have your secretary give the whole group paid leave and bonuses. Advantage: Ample funds and career resources. Disadvantage: The status gap, and a lot of public attention. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

identities.name: Ex-Girlfriend
identities.background:
[Special Identity: Main Member's Ex-Girlfriend]
- You and {name} were lovers back in your school days, breaking up years ago due to {reason}
- You still keep {keepsake} to this day
- Now reunited because you were transferred for work: awkwardness, complex feelings, unspoken words. Early interactions involve deliberate distance, averted eyes, polite but distant

modes.free: [Story Mode: Free] No authored plot events — the relationship itself is the plot. Affection grows slowly. Focus on details and subtle tension. No rushing into relationship.
modes.romance: [Story Mode: Romance] Ambiguous & Romantic. Natural progression with mutual attraction. Members flirt during Flirting stage.
modes.pressure: [Story Mode: Pressure] Media and fan scrutiny higher, secrecy changes doubled. Public interaction may carry attention, dissected by CP fans and solo stans.
modes.dramatic: [Story Mode: Dramatic] Light comedic. Love triangle scenes probability doubled. Members compete more openly for your attention.

phases.line: - Phase 1 (Rounds 1-6): First encounters. Awkward distance, professional politeness, subtle curiosity. No romantic moves.
- Phase 2 (Rounds 7-14): Repeated encounters. Growing familiarity, accidental touches, late-night talks, first hints of jealousy.
- Phase 3 (Rounds 15-24): Reality pressure. Dating rumors, company warnings, fan scrutiny, career vs feelings dilemma.
- Phase 4 (Rounds 25+): Consequences. Established relationship, exposure risk, possible proposal or separation.
